info.title: Puddle
info.description: Puddle's local API: pending requests, rules, audit, settings, consents and the event stream. Listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Every request needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (from the connection file), a `Host` of `127.0.0.1:<port>` or `localhost:<port>`, and no foreign `Origin`.

(PNG, JPEG or WebP, at most 8 MB, 32 to 8192 pixels on each side). It is checked and stored as
a 256 pixel square PNG, replacing an earlier one; one that is not square is fitted on a clear
square. This does not choose it: set `ui.app_icon` to `custom` for that.

post.summary:
Creates a workspace: its disk, then a clone of each repository in the list, one at a time.
The list is checked whole before anything exists. Each repository's identity joins the
workspace and its repository table row is made before the first clone. A clone that fails
fails only its repository: a background problem names it and the create still ends `done`.
Puddle picks the new workspace's id (eight random characters, never one used before); the
answer carries it. Answers 202; follow it with `workspace_progress` events.

checks.description: The checks, in a fixed order.

puddle_version.description: The Puddle version that ran the checks.

warn_foreign_credentials.description: Whether a credential Puddle did not add raises a warning.

wildcards_reach_local.description: Whether suffix rules reach local addresses.

oneOf.description:
Where in a request the stand-in is swapped. Left out: the secret's stored place when it

EnvSetRequest.description: What to set a variable to.

changed_at.description: When it last changed, epoch ms.

hosts.description:
The hosts a secret's real value may be sent to (names, or `*.` and a name for every name

overridden.description:
A global variable that the workspace's own variable of the same name hides. Only ever

oneOf.description: Where in a request a secret's stand-in is swapped; `null` for a plain variable.

value.description: A plain variable's value; `null` for a secret.

process.description: The killed process's name (`comm`), cleaned by [`Event::oom_kill`].

workspace.description: The workspace whose guest killed the process.

oneOf.description:
A disk of a workspace reached the warning threshold (`ui.disk_warning_percent`) or, with
the workspace still over it, grew fuller. Said once when a disk crosses the threshold and
again only after it has dropped below it.

percent.description: How full it is, in whole percent (rounded down), 0 to 100.

oneOf.description:
A workspace operation (create, start, stop, reclaim, reset the root disk, delete) moved on. An operation ends
with one event whose step is [`WorkspaceStep::Done`] or [`WorkspaceStep::Failed`].

detail.description:
More about the step, or why it failed; `null` when there is nothing to add. A cloning
step names the address. It can quote tool output: escape it when rendering.

oneOf.description: The checkout directory a cloning step is about; `null` for every other step.
A new open pending request (a workspace asked for a host:port no rule decides).
An open pending request was seen again.

attempts.description: Requests the row stands for now.

last_seen.description: Epoch ms of the latest one.

oneOf.description: A pending request is no longer open: decided by a user or by a rule, or expired.

rule_id.description: The rule that decided it; `null` for an expiry.

oneOf.description:
Rules were created, changed, deleted or expired. Global: every subscriber gets it (it
carries nothing, so each refetches what it may see).
A rule on method and path was created or deleted. Global: refetch `GET /api/request-rules`.

The list of identities, their order, the default or an identity's author or credentials
changed, or the Git defaults. Carries no data: refetch `GET /api/identities` (every
subscriber gets it, and each refetches its own).

A repository list Puddle renews in the background changed: a repository came or went, or
the list could not be read, or a Git host started or stopped limiting requests. Carries no
data: refetch `GET /api/repos`.

A workspace's identities, repository table or "only listed" switches changed (also when an
identity it has changed). Refetch `GET /api/workspaces/{id}/git`.

A global environment (the variables and secrets every workspace of one user gets) changed.
Carries no data: refetch `GET /api/env`, and a workspace's page refetches its own list too

A workspace's own environment changed. Refetch `GET /api/workspaces/{id}/env`. Never carries
a value.

A change to a workspace's environment could not be applied to it while it runs, or what a
deleted workspace held could not be removed. `reason` names the variable and says what is
wrong and what to do; it never holds a value. A workspace that runs keeps the secrets it
had; the change applies at its next start, or when the next change succeeds.

reason.description: What went wrong, for the user.

oneOf.description: A workspace's shell init was saved or removed. Refetch `GET /api/workspaces/{id}/shell-init`.

The workspace's own copy of its shell init (or the lines that load it) differed from the
host's when it started, and Puddle put the host's back. Something inside the workspace
changed it: tell the user.

A workspace's direct SSH did not work: its endpoint could not be opened or stopped
accepting, or a client's session ended with an error. `reason` says what failed and may
quote the runtime's error. The workspace keeps running; an `ssh` client that was refused
is told why on its own terminal.

reason.description: What went wrong, for the user.

oneOf.description:
A workspace's direct SSH accepts connections again after a [`Self::WorkspaceSshFailed`]
that said it kept trying. The app withdraws that notice.

A workspace's repository list changed (an entry was added, managed, cloned again or
removed). Carries nothing more: refetch `GET /api/workspaces/{id}` and its checkouts.

The ports a workspace listens on, its forwards or its pinned forwards changed. Carries no
data: refetch `GET /api/workspaces/{id}/ports`.

A forward could not be set up or kept: a pinned forward that could not be restored at the
workspace's start, or one whose port on this computer another program took. `reason` names
the port and, when known, who has it; it may quote the operating system's error.

reason.description: What went wrong and what to do, for the user.

oneOf.description:
A tool in a workspace that decrypts every host refused Puddle's certificate for `host`, so
Puddle stopped decrypting it and passes it through from now on (until the time is up or
the user decrypts it again). Refetch `GET /api/workspaces/{id}/interception/learned`.

count.description:
How many times Puddle has stopped decrypting this host in this workspace because a
tool refused its certificate, this one included. The app raises a notice from the
third time.

oneOf.description:
A workspace asked for a credential and the source of it cannot supply one (not signed in,
or the sign-in ran out). The user signs in from Puddle; a request never opens a sign-in
window. Global: it goes to the owner's streams. Names only, never a value.

host.description: The Git host the workspace was talking to.

source.description: The source, as one line of names (`gh account me on github.com`).

oneOf.description:
A push or a fetch was refused because the workspace's repository table does not allow it.
`host`, `owner` and `repo` are the table's spelling of the repository (lower-case, no
`.git`), so the notice can add the row as it is.

A Git host answered a workspace's request with `401` and no identity covers the owner, so
Puddle added no credential and the server's answer reached the workspace as it is. Sent
only when the workspace's own tool did not retry with a credential of its own soon after.
`repo` is the table's spelling, as in [`Event::GitAccessDenied`].

owner.description: The user or organisation no identity covers.

oneOf.description:
A login made inside a workspace could not be captured, or one Puddle kept could not be
used (`kind` says which). The service is one of Puddle's built-in login profiles, never
anything the guest sent. Names only, never a value.

service.description: The service as the user knows it (`Claude Code`, `GitHub`).

workspace.description: The workspace the login is in.

oneOf.description:
A request of the workspace carried a credential Puddle did not add or swap, and the
warning is on. The request went out as it was. `host` is the host it went to and `kind`
says what Puddle could tell about the credential; never a part of its value.

host.description: The host the request went to.

kind.description: What kind of credential it looked like.

oneOf.description:
An answer to a request of the workspace held a token of a known kind that Puddle does not
hold, and the warning is on. The answer went to the workspace as it was. `host` is the
host that sent it and `kind` says what the token looked like; never a part of its value.

kind.description: What kind of token it looked like.

workspace.description: The workspace that got the answer.

oneOf.description:
New audit records were committed. `id` is the newest record's id, so a client that holds
everything up to `after` reads on with `GET /api/audit?after=`. One event per commit and
user, not per record: it goes to the streams of the user the records belong to.

id.description: The newest audit record's id of that user.

oneOf.description:
The network or the system's proxy settings changed (after a quiet period), so what
`GET /api/network-health` showed may be out of date. Global: it goes to the owner's
streams.

epoch.description: The network epoch that began; it only grows while Puddle runs.

oneOf.description:
Signing in to the company proxy failed (it turned the credentials or the token down, or
asked again and again), so what `GET /api/network-health` lists under sign-in has changed.
Sent once when a proxy goes from signed in (or never tried) to failing, not on every retry.
Names the proxy and the scheme only, never a credential. Global: it goes to the owner's
streams.

scheme.description: The scheme that was sent (`Negotiate`, `NTLM`, `Basic`); `null` when none was.

oneOf.description:
The list of background problems changed (something Puddle does on its own failed, or the
cause went away). Carries no data: refetch `GET /api/problems`. Global: every
subscriber gets it (each refetches what it may see).

The free space on the drive that holds Puddle's data moved across the warning or the
failure line, or back above both (`level` is then `ok`). Sent when the level changes, not
on every read; the first read after Puddle starts counts as a change when it is not `ok`.
Global: it goes to the owner's streams.

free_mib.description: The free space at the read that changed the level, in whole MiB.

level.description: Where the free space stands now.

Event.description:
Something the user should hear about. Serialised as one internally tagged enum
(`{"type":"oom_kill",...}`, ADR 0002).

Most events are about one workspace and carry a `workspace` field; global ones (crash report
waiting, consent needed, network change, ...) carry none, and [`Event::workspace`] returns
`None` for them.

oneOf.description: One colour.

Fill.description: What a rule set is painted with: one solid colour today. A gradient would be another `kind`.

FindingList.description: A bounded list of lines from the unsaved-work check.

completed.description: The flow has been finished or skipped, so the app opens on its start screen.

completed_at.description: Epoch ms of that; `null` while it still has to run.

dev_certificate.description: What the certificates step says about a development certificate.

FirstRunRequest.description: Marks the first-run flow finished, or open again.

completed.description:
`true` records that the flow was finished or skipped (the time of the first such call is
kept); `false` makes it run again at the next start.

ForeignCredentialKind.description:
What Puddle can tell about a credential it did not add: by its bytes alone, never by whose it
is (the user's own token and a leaked one look the same). See [`Event::ForeignCredential`].

FoundAccount.description: An account that is already signed in on this computer. Names only.

org.description: The Azure DevOps organisation the account is bound to, when the listing says.

signed_in.description: False when the tool lists the account but its token no longer works.

FoundAccounts.description: What Puddle found signed in on this computer.

problems.description: The listings that could not run.

FoundProblem.description: A listing that could not run, so its accounts are missing from the list.

message.description: Why, in words ("gh is not installed or not on PATH").

GitAccess.description: What a workspace's repository table refused, as [`Event::GitAccessDenied`] reports it.

GitDefaultsView.description: The default of the two switches, for every workspace that has not set its own.

only_pull_listed.description: Refuse a fetch from a repository not listed with Pull on (built in: off).

only_push_listed.description: Refuse a push to a repository not listed with Push on (built in: on).

GitRepoRequest.description: Adds a repository to the table.

pull.description: A fetch from it may go out.

push.description: A push to it may go out.

repo.description: `repo`, or `project/repo` on Azure DevOps; `.git` is dropped.

pull.description: A fetch from it may go out.

push.description: A push to it may go out.

GitRepoView.description: One row of a workspace's repository table.

pull.description: A fetch from it may go out.

push.description: A push to it may go out.

repo.description: `repo`, or `project/repo` on Azure DevOps; lower-case, no `.git`.

GitSwitchesRequest.description: Sets either switch; a switch left out stays as it is.

never_decrypt.description: The names, as for a workspace; sorted. On saving, replaces the whole list. At most 500.

GlobalSettingsRequest.description: New global settings. Replaces every value listed here; unknown stored fields are kept.

GlobalSettingsView.description: The global settings, and what a workspace without overrides gets.

effective.description: The effective values for a workspace with no overrides.

unknown_fields.description:
Fields in the stored document this Puddle doesn't know (written by a newer one); they
are kept.

size_mib.description:
The new root disk size in MiB. It must be above the current size: a root disk only grows.
Required.

Health.description: The API's identity, for a client to check it reached Puddle.

ui_build_id.description:
The build of the app this server serves, read from the build's own `_app/version.json`: a
page that carries another build is stale and reloads. `null` when the server serves no
app (a development server behind the Vite proxy).

IdentityAuthor.description: The name and email git writes into a commit.

IdentityCredentialView.description:
A credential of an identity as the host shows it: the reference and what the last read of it
came to.

oneOf.description: The last read of its source since Puddle started; `null` before any.

detached_from.description: The workspaces it was taken off.

tokens_left.description:
The pasted tokens it read that no other identity reads and that the credential store would
not give up (it is locked or unreachable). They stay there until the sweep at the next
start; empty when every token went.

IdentityOrderRequest.description: The order of the identities: every id once.

credentials.description: Its credentials. No two of one identity may cover the same place.

label.description: The name you see; unique whatever the case.

credentials.description: Its credentials, as references, with the last read of each.

is_default.description: Whether it is the default: what a new workspace gets when no identity covers its URL.

Inbox.description: The inbox: open requests grouped by registrable domain, most recent group first.

open_limit.description:
The most open requests Puddle lists for one workspace. A workspace with this many has a
full list: a new host it asks about is answered as waiting but gets no row until the user
answers some (rules spec R-45).

InboxGroup.description: Open requests that share a registrable domain (R-18). Grouping is for display only.

InterceptionMode.description:
Which hosts on port 443 Puddle decrypts, beyond the ones with a credential, secret, login
capture profile or rule on method and path (those are always decrypted).

InterceptionRequest.description: A change to a workspace's interception. A field that is absent stays as it is.

oneOf.description: Sets the workspace's own mode. It applies to the running workspace at once.

never_decrypt.description:
Replaces the workspace's never-decrypt names. Each is a host name or `*.` followed by a
domain with at least two labels; no IP addresses. At most 500.

InterceptionSettingsRequest.description: A change to the global interception setting. A field that is absent stays as it is.

learn_from_rejections.description: Turns learning from rejections on or off.

oneOf.description: Chooses the mode.

notice_seen.description: Records that the user has seen the notice.

chosen.description: Whether the user has chosen a mode. While `false`, the app offers the choice once.

curated.description:
The curated list passed through in `all_except_curated`: built in, "System managed",
sorted.

learn_from_rejections.description:
Whether a host whose tool refuses Puddle's certificate is passed through for a while and
put on the learned list. Meaningful in the modes that decrypt unlisted hosts. On unless
turned off.

mode.description:
The mode every workspace without its own follows. An install that has not chosen is on
`known_only`.

notice_seen.description: Whether the user has seen the notice that offers the choice (existing installs).

InterceptionView.description:
How a workspace decrypts hosts beyond the ones it has a credential, secret, login capture or
rule on method and path for.

effective_mode.description: The mode in force: the workspace's own, or the global one.

global_never_decrypt.description: The names no workspace decrypts, sorted. Changed through the global route.

mode.description: The workspace's own choice; `inherit` follows the global setting.

never_decrypt.description:
The names this workspace never decrypts while it decrypts unlisted hosts (`example.com`,
`*.example.com`), sorted.

InviteRequest.description: Uses an invite link (made by the server's command line) to set a password.

device_name.description: What this browser calls itself in the device list; `null` for the default.

password.description: The new password: at least 12 characters.

secret.description: The secret after `#` in the invite link.

KeptLoginList.description: The logins kept for a workspace. No token, stand-in or account detail is in it.

logins.description: The services with a login kept; empty when none is.

store_readable.description:
`false` when the operating system's credential store did not answer and Puddle had no
record of its own: `logins` is then empty because it is not known, not because nothing is
kept.

KeptLoginView.description: A service Puddle keeps a login for in a workspace.

name.description: What the user calls it: `Claude Code`, `GitHub`.

service.description: The service as forgetting names it: `claude` or `github`.

since.description:
When Puddle first noted the login as kept, epoch ms; `null` when it does not know (the
login was kept before Puddle wrote times down).

Lagged.description:
Sent on the event stream as `event: lagged` when a subscriber fell behind and events were
dropped for it. The client should refetch the state it shows.

LastCheck.description: What the last read of a credential came to, wherever the read came from. Never the value.

fix_step.description: The exact step the user takes to fix it, when there is one; `null` otherwise.

needs_sign_in.description: True when the way out is for the user to sign in.

problem.description: Why not, in words; `null` when it is readable.

readable.description: True when the source gave a value.

LearnedHost.description: A host a tool in a workspace refused Puddle's certificate for.

count.description:
How many times Puddle stopped decrypting the host after a refusal. From the third time on
the app suggests making the host permanent.

expires_in_secs.description: Seconds until Puddle decrypts the host again by itself; `null` unless `passed_through`.

first_rejected_at.description: When a tool first refused the certificate for this host, milliseconds since the epoch.

last_rejected_at.description: When a tool last refused it, milliseconds since the epoch.

passed_through.description:
Whether Puddle passes the host through now. `false` once the time is up or the user
decrypted it again (the host stays listed with its history), and for a workspace that is
not running: nothing is passed through then.

LearnedHosts.description: The hosts a workspace's tools refused Puddle's certificate for.

hosts.description:
The hosts passed through now first, soonest to expire first; then the others, the most
recently refused first. The history is kept in the database; the pass-through is held in
memory by the running workspace, so a start begins with none passed through.

LearnedLimits.description:
How long and how many hosts Puddle passes through after a tool refused its certificate. The
same for every workspace.

cap.description: Hosts remembered per workspace, 1 to 10 000; the oldest makes room. Built in: 1024.

ttl_secs.description: Seconds a host is passed through, 60 to 2 592 000 (30 days). Built in: 43 200 (12 hours).

LocalCategory.description:
A class of local destination with its own toggle. Everything outside these is public.

A toggle only *permits* its category; each destination still needs an allow rule or an
approval. Puddle's own endpoints are not a category: no toggle reaches them.

Non-exhaustive: more categories may follow.

LocalToggles.description: Local destination categories a workspace may approve. `null` inherits.

company_network.description: The company network. Off by default; on only makes those destinations approvable.

LoginProblemKind.description: What is wrong with a login, as [`Event::LoginProblem`] reports it.

scope.description: Which never-decrypt list gets the host.

NetworkHealth.description: `GET /api/network-health`: everything Puddle knows about how it reaches the internet.

company_network.description: What drives the company-network destination category.

generated_at.description: Epoch ms the report was made.

routes.description: Routes chosen so far in this network epoch, sorted by host (at most 100).

directory.description:
The checkout's directory under the volume root; left out or `null` is the folder's name
for a `local_path`, else the last part of the address (`api` for
`https://github.com/acme/api.git`), or `src` when that is no usable name.

identity_id.description:
The identity that serves it (`id` of `GET /api/identities`); left out or `null` is the
identity that covers its owner, else the default identity.

local_path.description:
A git checkout on this computer to start from, as an absolute path to its folder (or its
`.git`). Only its `.git` directory is read, read-only, by a short-lived sandbox with no
network that clones it: every commit, branch and tag comes along; uncommitted changes and
untracked files (an `.env`) stay on this computer. The clone's `origin` is `url`. A
worktree's or submodule's `.git` file and a bare repository are refused with the reason.

pull.description:
Pull on its new repository table row; left out or `null` is on. A row the table already
has keeps its toggles.

push.description: Push on its new repository table row; left out or `null` is on.

url.description:
The repository to clone, as an `https://` URL without credentials. SSH remotes
(`git@host:path`, `ssh://`) are refused with a message saying so. With `local_path` it
may be left out or empty: the checkout's `origin` remote gives it (an SSH remote of
GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket or Azure DevOps in its HTTPS form).

NewRequestRuleRequest.description: A rule on method and path to make.

host.description: A host name or `*.` followed by a domain with at least two labels; no IP address.

methods.description:
HTTP methods (letters and digits, case does not matter); left out or empty for every
method. At most 16.

path.description:
The path: `/` followed by segments, where `*` is one whole segment and a closing `/**` is
everything below. No query string. It is compared after percent-decoding, with `.` and
`..` resolved and case ignored.

oneOf.description: The workspace the rule applies to; `null` for every workspace.

NewRuleRequest.description: A rule to create directly (not from a pending request).

expires_at.description: Epoch ms from which the rule no longer matches; left out or `null` is permanent.

pattern.description:
`example.com` (exact), or `.example.com` / `*.example.com` (suffix; a public suffix is
refused).

oneOf.description: The colour; left out for the default of the set's number.

name.description: 1 to 64 characters, not used by another set.

NewWorkspaceIdentity.description:
What the Git settings of one repository of a new workspace started with. Only the answer to
creating a workspace carries it; the Git tab shows the same thing afterwards.

identity.description: The label of the identity it got; `null` for none.

warning.description:
What to tell you when no identity covers the repository (which one it got and what that
means); `null` when one does.

NewWorkspaceIdentityBasis.description: Why a new workspace's repository got the identity it got.

image.description: The image to boot; left out or `null` is the default devcontainer image.

memory_mib.description: Memory in MiB (256 to 1048576); left out or `null` is the default.

name.description:
What the user calls the workspace: display text of 1 to 60 characters, spaces at the
ends dropped, no line breaks or control characters. Another live workspace's name (ignoring
case) is `409`. The answer carries the new workspace's `id`.

repositories.description:
The repositories to clone, in order (0 to 100); left out is none. The list is checked
whole before anything exists.

start_folder.description:
Where new terminals land and what the editor opens: a path under the volume (relative,
`/` between its parts, at most 255 bytes, not inside `.puddle`); left out or `null` is the
volume root.

OrphanVolumeList.description: The workspace disks the list does not name, in id order.

volumes.description: Empty when the list names every workspace disk.

OrphanVolumeView.description:
A workspace disk Puddle keeps whose workspace its list does not name. Puddle cannot tell from
outside whether the disk holds any files, so none of this says so.

id.description: The id a restore names; also the name of the workspace a restore makes.

volume.description: The disk's name in the runtime, `ws-` and the id.

PacState.description: Whether the PAC script or WPAD answered.

PaletteChoice.description: Which colour palette the window uses over the light or dark base.

device_name.description: What this browser calls itself in the device list; `null` for the default.

PendingRequest.description: A connection that matched no rule and waits for the user (R-10).

attempts.description: How many requests the row stands for.

oneOf.description:
For an open request to a local destination (host loopback, private network, link-local,
metadata, special) whose toggle is off in this workspace: the toggle that blocks approval.
An allow rule would not let the connection through until the toggle is on. `null`
otherwise, and always for a closed request.

company_signal.description:
For an open request to an IP literal on the company network, whether or not its toggle is
on: what put the address there (`pac_direct`, `dns_suffix`, `private_access_cgnat` or
`vpn_route`). `null` otherwise. A client that reads the address ranges itself needs it to
tell a company address from the plain range it also falls in.

decided_at.description: Epoch ms it was decided or expired.

oneOf.description: Who closed it.

first_seen.description: Epoch ms of the first request.

host.description:
The requested host: a normalised name (punycode, lower case) or an IP literal. Untrusted
(it comes from the guest): escape it when rendering.

last_seen.description: Epoch ms of the latest request.

rule_set.description:
The rule set whose entry decided it (`system`, `builtin:<slug>`, `user:<id>`), when one
did.

state.description: Where the row is in its life.

PendingState.description: Where a pending request is in its life (R-12).

PendingSummary.description:
An open pending request as [`Event::PendingOpened`] carries it. `host` comes from the guest
(already normalised by the proxy): escape it when rendering.

first_seen.description: Epoch ms of the first request.

last_seen.description: Epoch ms of the latest one.

registrable_domain.description:
The host's registrable domain (`example.co.uk` for `api.example.co.uk`; the IP literal
itself), the key the inbox groups rows by.

PermanentScope.description: Where a learned host is never decrypted from now on.

forwarded.description: A forward to it is open now: connecting to `host_port` on this computer reaches it.

host_port.description:
The port on this computer: the open forward's, or the one a pinned forward wants. `null`
for a port that is neither forwarded nor pinned.

listening.description:
A process in the workspace listens on it now. Reported by the workspace itself, so a
workspace that is not running lists none, and one that hides a listener hides it here.

pinned.description: The forward comes back, on the same `host_port`, every time the workspace starts.

problem.description:
Why it does not work: the pinned forward could not be restored (the port of this computer
is in use, and by whom), or the last connection through it failed. May quote the guest's
or the system's words: escape it when rendering. `null` when there is no problem.

PortForwardRequest.description: Forwards a port of the workspace to this computer.

host_port.description: The port on this computer, 1 to 65535. Left out or `null`: the workspace port's own number.

pinned.description:
Keep the forward across restarts of the workspace (default false). Asking again with
`true` pins a forward that is open; with `false` it unpins one and leaves it open until
the workspace stops.

Problem.description: One background problem, as `GET /api/problems` lists it.

detail.description:
What Puddle did about it and what the user can do. It can quote tool output: escape it
when rendering.

key.description:
Names the problem; raising it again replaces the old one, and it ends with
[`Problems::clear`].

title.description: What went wrong, in one line. It can quote tool output: escape it when rendering.

oneOf.description: The workspace it is about, or `null` when it is about Puddle.

ProxyDetected.description: What Puddle found out about the proxy setup.

ProxyMode.description: Where Puddle gets its proxy setting from.

ProxyProblem.description: One thing in the proxy setup that does not work as the user set it up.

detail.description: Which setting or part, and why, as a sentence fragment; contains no credential.

ProxyProblemKind.description: What kind of trouble a [`ProxyProblem`] is.

bypass_entries.description: How many destinations the fixed settings exempt (the bypass list's length).

epoch.description: The network epoch; it grows each time a network or settings change is noticed.

http_proxy.description: The fixed proxy for plain HTTP (`host:port`), or `null`.

https_proxy.description: The fixed proxy for HTTPS (`host:port`), or `null`.

last_change_at.description: Epoch ms when the last change was noticed; `null` when none since Puddle started.

pac_state.description: Whether the PAC or WPAD answered.

pac_url.description: The PAC script's address, without user info, query or fragment; `null` when none.

problems.description: What in the setup does not work as set, one entry each; empty when all does.

settings_error.description: Why the system settings, or a part of them, could not be read; `null` when they could.

ProxySignInList.description: The proxies Puddle holds a sign-in for.

ProxySignInRequest.description: Stores or replaces the sign-in for one proxy.

password.description:
The password: not empty, no line break. Written once to the operating system's credential
store and never shown again.

proxy.description: The proxy as `host:port`, or `http://host:port`; a missing port is 80.

user.description:
The user name: not empty, at most 256 bytes, no colon or line break (Basic cannot carry
them).

PullProxyReport.description: Image pulls and the pull proxy.

active.description: Image pulls go through Puddle's pull proxy (where the rules and the guard apply).

via_upstream.description: The pull proxy reaches the internet through the company proxy setup above.

RemoteNote.description: Why a checkout's remote address is not shown as it stands.

name.description:
The new name: 1 to 60 characters, spaces at the ends dropped, no line breaks or control
characters. Required.

RepoFindings.description: What one checkout holds that is not on a remote.

clean.description: Whether nothing in it would be lost.

dir.description: The checkout's directory in the workspace.

uncommitted.description: Uncommitted changes and untracked files (`git status --porcelain` lines).

RepoListState.description: How current one credential's list is.

RepoListing.description:
The repositories of the identities, one entry each, by name, and how current each credential's
list is.

limit.description: The page size that was applied.

repos.description: The matching repositories, a page of them.

sources.description:
One entry per credential (per organisation on Azure DevOps) of the identities asked for,
in the identities' order. Read these before trusting an empty `repos`.

total.description: How many repositories match, before the page is cut.

RepoNote.description: A fact about a list or a profile, in words.

RepoNoteCode.description: What a list or a profile leaves out.

RepoProblem.description: A reason in words, with what to do about it.

message.description: What happened and the way out. Never a secret.

needs_sign_in.description: Whether signing in again is the way out.

RepoProblemCode.description: Why a list or a profile could not be read.

identity_id.description: Only this identity's credentials; leave out (or `null`) for every identity's.

RepoRole.description:
What the account that lists a repository can do in it, as the host says. A fine-grained token
can hold less than the account's role.

RepoSource.description:
One credential's list (for an Azure DevOps credential, one organisation's) and how current it
is. An empty list with no problem means the account reaches no repository.

credential.description: The credential's place in that identity's list (from 0).

identity_id.description: The identity that holds the credential.

organisation.description: The Azure DevOps organisation this list is for; `null` elsewhere.

oneOf.description: Why the newest read is missing or failed; `null` when it worked.

refreshed_at.description: Epoch ms the list was read; `null` when it never was.

repo_count.description: How many repositories the list holds.

retry_at.description: Epoch ms the host lets Puddle ask again, when it said to wait.

RepoSources.description: How current each list is after a refresh. Read the repositories with `GET /api/repos`.

sources.description: One entry per credential (per organisation on Azure DevOps) asked for.

RepoView.description: A repository an identity can reach.

full_name.description: `owner/name`, or `organisation/project/name` on Azure DevOps: what a search matches.

identities.description:
The identities whose credentials list it; the first listed it first. Offer these to
"create a workspace for this".

owner.description: The user or organisation that owns it; the organisation on Azure DevOps.

role.description: What the account can do in it.

url.description: The HTTPS address to clone, with no user name: what the create form takes.

blocked_by.description: For `blocked`: which rule or rule set blocks it, in words; `null` otherwise.

RepositoryHostState.description: Where a repository host stands with the rules.

RepositoryHosts.description: The hosts of the addresses, in the order they first appear, each once.

RepositoryHostsRequest.description: `POST /api/repository-hosts`: the repositories of a create form, or of a repository to add.

urls.description:
The repository addresses. One that is not an HTTPS address of a repository has no host
here; the create refuses it by itself.

workspace.description: The workspace the repositories are for; leave it out for one that does not exist yet.

RequestRule.description:
A rule on method and path. It only refuses: the requests it names to a host Puddle decrypts
are answered with a 403 and never leave the computer. The host is always decrypted for it.

id.description: Row id, never reused. Numbered apart from the rules on hosts.

methods.description: The methods it names, upper case; empty for every method.

path.description:
The path pattern in canonical form: `/a/b`, with `*` for one segment and a closing `/**`
for everything below.

warning.description:
Set when the rule's host is on a never-decrypt list the rule applies under (the global
one, and the workspace's own or, for a global rule, any workspace's): the rule decrypts the
host anyway, so a tool there that does not trust Puddle's certificate fails on it. Names
the names it overrides; `null` when it overrides none.

oneOf.description: The workspace it applies to; `null` for every workspace.

ResolvedBool.description: An effective on/off value and where it came from.

ResolvedClipboardRead.description: The effective clipboard-read setting and where it came from.

ResolvedNumber.description: An effective number (MiB or seconds, see the field) and where it came from.

repository.description:
The address of the repository on the disk, used only when Puddle cannot read one from the
remote of a checkout there. An HTTPS address; an SSH one is refused as in a create.

RootsReport.description: The company roots Puddle copied into workspaces.

left_out_of_tls.description:
Company certificates Puddle's own TLS checks could not use (the checks that guard a
workspace's credentials on the way out): a server that chains to one fails with an unknown
issuer. Workspaces still get them; this is only about what Puddle itself verifies.

roots.description: How many trust anchors workspaces get.

synced.description:
Whether the host's certificate stores have been read (false until the first sync, and
on systems where Puddle has no store to read).

synced_at.description: Epoch ms of the last read; `null` when none.

unreadable_stores.description: Stores that could not be read, with the system's reason.

RouteDecision.description: The route Puddle chose for one destination in this network epoch.

hops.description: The hops in order: `PROXY host:port` or `DIRECT`.

host.description: The host, from a guest request: escape it.

expires_at.description: Epoch ms from which the rule no longer matches; `null` is permanent.

source_pending_id.description: The pending request it was decided from.

expires_at.description: Epoch ms in the future, or `null` to make the rule permanent.

RuleList.description: Every rule, expired ones the sweeper hasn't removed yet included.

oneOf.description: Every workspace.
One workspace.

and workspace rules decide first.

RuleScope.description: Which workspaces a rule applies to.

RuleSetEntry.description: One entry of a rule set.

effect.description: Allow or deny (a built-in set's entries all do the same; your own set may mix them).

expires_at.description: Epoch ms from which the entry no longer counts; `null` is permanent.

note.description: What it is for (built-in sets); empty for your own entries.

pattern.description:
`example.com`, or `.example.com` for every name under it (a built-in entry is written
`*.example.com`).

rule_id.description: The entry's rule, for a set you made (delete or change it through `/api/rules`).

RuleSetList.description: Every rule set, and the System managed hosts.

sets.description: Built-in sets first, then yours by name.

system_managed.description:
The hosts Puddle allows because of your setup, each with its reason. Your own rules
decide first: a deny of yours blocks one.

RuleSetOverride.description: One workspace's own switch for a set.

RuleSetSwitchRequest.description: Switch a set on or off, for every workspace or for one.

enabled.description:
On or off; `null` removes the switch, so the next level decides (the global switch, then
the set's default).

oneOf.description: The workspace whose own switch to set; left out or `null` for every workspace.

closed.description: Open requests the set now decides, closed the same way.

set.description: The set as it is now.

RuleSetUpdateRequest.description: A rule set's new name, description and colour.

oneOf.description: The new colour; left out keeps the one the set has.

name.description: 1 to 64 characters, not used by another set.

RuleSetView.description: A rule set: where it is on, and its entries.

changed_at.description: Built-in sets: epoch ms when a Puddle update last changed the entries; `null` if never.

created_at.description: Your sets: epoch ms it was made.

default_on.description: Whether it is on where nobody switched it: built-in sets ship off, your sets start on.

fill.description:
The colour it is shown in: a built-in set's own, or the one you chose (a set you made
without choosing has a default of its number).

global.description: The switch for every workspace; `null` follows `default_on`.

overrides.description: Workspaces with a switch of their own.

SandboxName.description: A sandbox's name: a DNS label (`a-z`, `0-9`, `-`, no leading or trailing `-`).

ScopeChoice.description: Whether an approval or denial covers only the request's workspace or every workspace.

oneOf.description: The values of request headers: what almost every tool uses.

The one query parameter `name` (`appid`, `access_token`, `key`), for an API that takes its
key nowhere else.

name.description: The parameter's name: 1 to 64 visible characters, none of `&`, `=`, `#`, `%`, `+`.

oneOf.description: The path (a Telegram bot's `/bot<token>/`, a webhook URL).

SecretPlace.description:
Where in a request Puddle swaps a secret's stand-in for its real value, toward the secret's
hosts only. Anywhere else the stand-in goes out unchanged.

ServerChoice.description: Which VS Code server browser VS Code runs.

SessionGrant.description:
What a sign-in or a refresh gives the browser: an access token to send as
`Authorization: Bearer` for the next 15 minutes. The long-lived part, the refresh token, is
never in a body: it is in an `HttpOnly` cookie the page cannot read.

access_token.description: The access token. Keep it in memory only.

device.description: This browser's entry in the device list.

expires_at.description: When it stops working, epoch ms; ask for a new one before.

SettingSource.description: Which level an effective value came from.

SettingsLayer.description:
The settings every workspace has. On a global document they are the defaults for every
workspace; on a workspace they override those. `null` means "not set here": the next level (the
global value, then Puddle's default) applies.

capture_logins.description:
Whether a login made inside the workspace (Claude Code, `gh`, Copilot CLI) is captured:
Puddle keeps the real token on the host and the workspace holds a stand-in that works
only through Puddle. On by default; applies at the workspace's next start.

oneOf.description: What a programmatic clipboard read does.

cpus.description: Guest vCPUs (1 to 32); applies at the next start.

direct_ssh.description:
Whether Puddle opens an SSH way into the workspace for the user's own tools (desktop
VS Code, a terminal `ssh`). Off by default; while off there is no SSH endpoint and no ssh
config entry. Turning it on marks the workspace trusted.

local_toggles.description: Which local destination categories may be approved (all off by default).

memory.description: Guest memory in MiB (256 to 1 048 576); applies at the next start.

reconnection_grace.description: Seconds a browser VS Code session survives a disconnect (30 to 86 400).

warn_foreign_credentials.description:
Whether Puddle warns when a request carries a credential it did not add (a token the
workspace holds itself). The request goes out either way; this only switches the notice
and the flag in the activity log. On by default.

wildcards_reach_local.description: Whether a suffix rule may reach local addresses.

zoom_hotkeys.description: Whether the browser window's zoom hotkeys work.

SetupRequest.description: The first visitor makes the owner account.

device_name.description: What this browser calls itself in the device list; `null` for the default.

content.description:
The whole script. Line ends become LF. At most 48 KiB, no NUL, not empty (to remove the
shell init, delete it).

checked.description:
Whether the script was run in a throwaway shell in the running workspace and printed
nothing. `false` when the workspace is not running: Puddle checks it when it starts, and
says so as a problem if it fails then.

unchecked_reason.description: Why it was not checked, when `checked` is `false`.

ShellInitView.description: The shell init saved for a workspace.

changed_at.description: When it was last saved, epoch ms; `null` when none is saved.

content.description: The script; empty when none is saved.

saved.description: Whether one is saved. A workspace with none starts all the same.

SignInAttempt.description: The latest sign-in attempt to one proxy.

detail.description: More, in words; `null` when there is nothing to add.

scheme.description: The scheme sent (`Negotiate`, `NTLM`, `Basic`); `null` when none was.

SignInMethodRequest.description: Switches one method on or off. The last method that is on can't be switched off.

SignInMethodView.description: One sign-in method and whether it is on.

SignInReport.description: How Puddle signs in to the company proxy.

attempts.description: The latest attempt per proxy, newest first.

methods.description:
The schemes Puddle can answer a proxy with, lower case (`negotiate`, `ntlm`, `basic`).

stored.description:
The proxies Puddle holds a stored user name and password for (Basic), sorted by proxy.

source.description: The credential to sign in to.

SignInResult.description: How a sign-in to a proxy ended.

SignInStarted.description:
What the user does to finish a sign-in Puddle started. Poll the credential's check to learn
when it worked; Puddle ends a sign-in nobody finished after five minutes.

code.description: The one-time code to type at `url`; `null` when the tool opens its own window.

url.description: Where to type it; `null` when the tool opens its own window.

SkippedRoot.description: A certificate in the host's stores that workspaces do not get.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the certificate, lower-case hex.

subject.description: The subject's common name, when readable.

keys.description:

`null` for every key the agent holds.

changed_at.description: Epoch ms the agent was turned on for the host, or its keys last changed.

host.description: The host, as `ssh` in the workspace names it: a lower-case name or an IP address.

keys.description:
The keys it may use, as SHA-256 fingerprints (`SHA256:...`, as `ssh-keygen -l` prints
them), sorted; `null` for every key the agent holds.

SshAgentView.description: The hosts a workspace may use the user's SSH agent for. Empty unless the user turned it on.

path.description:
The folder, relative to the workspace's volume: parts joined by `/`, none empty, `.` or
`..`, no control character or `\`, not inside `.puddle` or `lost+found`, at most 255
bytes. It may name a folder that does not exist yet. `null` is the volume root. Required,
so an empty body never resets it.

StartFolderSet.description: The start folder after a change.

exists.description:
Whether the folder exists in the workspace: `true` or `false` while it runs, `null` when it
is stopped (Puddle looks when it starts) or the start folder is the volume root. A folder
that is missing opens the volume root and shows a problem until it exists.

start_folder.description: The start folder now; `null` is the volume root.

StoreTokenRequest.description:
A token the user pasted. It is kept in the operating system's credential store under Puddle's
own name and never read back through the API.

host.description: The Git host the token is for.

org.description: The organisation, for tokens that belong to one (Azure DevOps).

StoredSignIn.description: A stored proxy sign-in. Names only.

user.description: The user name the proxy is signed in to with.

StoredToken.description: Where a stored token went: the source to put in a credential.

source.description: A `stored` source naming the new entry.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the certificate, lower-case hex.

sources.description: The stores it was found in (`LocalMachine\Root\.GroupPolicy`).

TerminalRequest.description: The size a new terminal starts with.

org.description: The organisation, for tokens that belong to one (Azure DevOps).

badge.description: The waiting count on the tray, taskbar and window title (default on).

oneOf.description: What the close button does (default `tray`).

confirm_global_rules.description: Ask before a decision creates a rule for every workspace (default on).

custom_accent.description: The `custom` palette's accent colour, `#rrggbb`; `null` keeps Pond's.

custom_background.description: The `custom` palette's page background, `#rrggbb`; `null` keeps Pond's.

custom_surface.description: The `custom` palette's cards and panels, `#rrggbb`; `null` keeps Pond's.

oneOf.description:
Comfortable or compact spacing for the whole app (default `comfortable`). A request may
leave it out, like every field here: out or `null` means the default.

disk_fail_free_gb.description:
The free space, in GB, under which `puddle doctor` fails; 1 to 10000, default 5, never above
the warning line.

disk_warn_free_gb.description:
The free space, in GB (1024 x 1024 x 1024 bytes), under which `puddle doctor` warns and the
app says so; 1 to 10000, default 20.

disk_warning_percent.description:
How full a workspace's root disk or volume gets, in percent, before Puddle warns on the
workspace and, with `notify_disk_full`, notifies; 50 to 100 (default 95).

inbox_shortcuts.description: The inbox's single-key shortcuts A, D, J and K (default off).

minimize_to_tray.description: Minimizing hides the window to the tray instead of the taskbar (default off).

notifications.description: A system notification for a new request (default on).

notify_disk_full.description: Notify when a workspace's root disk or volume reaches `disk_warning_percent` (default on).

notify_low_disk_space.description:
Notify when the free space on the drive that holds Puddle's data falls under the warning or
the failure line (default on).

notify_only_unfocused.description: Notify only while Puddle's window is not focused (default on).

notify_oom.description: Notify when a workspace is killed for running out of memory (default on).

notify_unexpected_stop.description: Notify when a workspace stops or crashes without being asked to (default on).

oneOf.description: The colour palette over the light or dark base (default `pond`).

sound.description: The system sound with a notification (default off).

start_at_login.description: Start Puddle when the user signs in to the computer (default off).

oneOf.description: Light, dark or follow the system (default `system`).

UnknownTokenKind.description:
What Puddle can tell about a token in an answer that it does not hold: by its bytes alone

VsCodeServer.description: Options for the VS Code server in the guest. `null` means Puddle's default.

oneOf.description:

telemetry.description: Whether the server may send Microsoft telemetry (default off).

user put there), and the sandbox that runs it.

rule decided them (each is a rule made by the create, on the Rules screen). Only those
answers fill it; every other answer has an empty list.

oneOf.description: The operation in progress; `null` when idle.

direct_ssh.description:
Whether direct SSH is on for this workspace (its effective setting, `direct_ssh` in the
settings). The workspace is then "trusted": desktop VS Code and other SSH tools can
connect, and what runs in the workspace can reach this computer through them.

disk_size_mib.description: The disk's size in MiB: the most the workspace can hold.

disk_used_mib.description: What the disk holds in MiB; `null` when not known.

disk_warnings.description:
Which disks are at or over the warning threshold (`ui.disk_warning_percent` in the global
settings): `root`, `volume`, both or neither.

first_connect_notice_due.description:
Deprecated and always `false`: the first-connect notice is the "Allow direct SSH"
confirmation now. Read `direct_ssh` instead.

id.description:
The id every path, query parameter, event and rule scope uses. It never changes; a
rename changes `name` only.

identities.description:
Which identity each repository of a new workspace got and why, one per repository of the
request, in its order. Only the answer to creating a workspace fills it; every other answer
has an empty list, and the Git tab shows the same afterwards.

memory_mib.description: Memory in MiB, applied at the next start.

name.description:

`PATCH /api/workspaces/{id}`. It names nothing else; use `id` for that.

repositories.description: The repositories Puddle manages for it, in the order they were added (0 to 100).

root_disk_size_mib.description:
The root disk's size in MiB: the most the home directory, tool caches and installed
packages can take. `null` when not known.

What the root disk holds in MiB; `null` when not known. A root disk that is nearly full
can be reset (`POST /api/workspaces/{id}/reset-root-disk`).

session_user.description:
The guest user its sessions, browser editor and clones run as: `agent` (with passwordless
`sudo`) for a workspace made since non-root sessions came in, `root` for one made before or
switched back. A change applies at the next start (`PUT
/api/workspaces/{id}/session-user`).

settings_error.description:
Why `direct_ssh` is only a guess: the settings could not be read, so it counts as off.
`null` when the settings were read.

start_folder.description:
Where new terminals land and what the editor opens: a path under the volume, or `null`
for the volume root.

the workspace's own of the same name hides is listed after it with `overridden` set. The
workspace's environment is read when it starts: a change reaches a running workspace's own
environment at its next start; a secret's hosts and value apply at once.

identities.description: Its identities in order (the order breaks author ties; coverage picks the credential).

only_pull_listed.description: Refuse a fetch from a repository not listed with Pull on (default off).

only_push_listed.description: Refuse a push to a repository not listed with Push on (default on).

message.description: Names both workspaces and asks for the id.

`workspace_progress` events.

ports.description: The ports, by number: the ones that listen, the ones forwarded, the ones pinned.

running.description:

only.

the workspace's Git settings (`GET /api/workspaces/{id}/git`), matched in the repository
table's spelling.

directory.description: The checkout it is cloned into, directly under the volume root.

entry.description:

and the `clone:<id>:<entry>` problem key use. It never changes while the entry is on the
list.

url.description: The HTTPS address it is cloned from, without credentials.

WorkspaceSettingsRequest.description: New overrides for one workspace. Replaces every value listed; `null` inherits.

WorkspaceSettingsView.description: One workspace's overrides and effective values.

unknown_fields.description: Unknown fields in its stored document (kept).

WorkspaceStatus.description: A workspace's state: its sandbox's state as the runtime reports it (msb's states, one for one).

WorkspaceStep.description: Where a long workspace operation is, as [`Event::WorkspaceProgress`] reports it.
